newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish Metorex eyes Nasdaq in 1998. [CORRECTED 13:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Finnish Metorex eyes Nasdaq in 1998. [CORRECTED 13:00 GMT]

text.p: Metorex Oy, an unlisted Finnish manufacturer of scanning and material analysis equipment, plans to seek a listing on the U.S. Nasdaq or on Europe's Easdaq in 1998, Metorex managing director Tuula Lukander said on Thursday.
The company is not keen on a domestic listing because it is better known abroad than in Finland, Lukander told Reuters in an interview.
Metorex was bought out by its management from metals and mining group Outokumpu Oy in 1994.
It is completing a 30 million markka placement of shares and a capital loan to private foreign and Finnish investors but further ahead it will need more capital, Lukander said.
"There are potential corporate acquisitions ... and acquisitions of product licenses and technology," she said.
Metorex's new owners were looking at Nasdaq but Easdaq would also be an option if it became an efficient enough market by 1998, she said.
More than 96 percent of the company's net sales come from overseas but most of the production takes place in Finland.
Metorex makes X-ray detectors and analysis tools based on spectroscope technology.
It sees its greatest potential in security equipment, such as a new system to scan trucks, which it has submitted to a Finnish customs tender.
"Security is where (potential) is biggest... the market is growing faster than normal markets," Lukander said.
Metorex forecasts consolidated net sales surging to 375 million markka in 2000 from 105 million in 1995 and pretax profits rising to 15 million from a two million loss in 1995.
The year just started (corrects from ended) will bring a slight profit, but if R&D input for future products were credited to assets, profits would already be "significant", Lukander said.

After the placement -- to a consortium led by U.S.-Swiss Vision Capital which is an investment fund in the making -- Lukander's and her partner Heikki Sipila's holdings in Metorex will fall to 25.5 percent each from 30 percent.
Finnish state-controlled venture capital fund Sitra aims to sell its 40 percent stake, so the consortium will hold some 49 percent of the firm if the placement is fully subscribed.
Lukander said the placement outcome will be clear during January.
